svg.text: $ swift run UnitClaimDemo (complete output)
UnitClaimKit demo: stated unit conversions, recomputed exactly
[1] A recipe, converted for a metric kitchen
answer: "Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Whisk 2 cups of flour (500 g) with 1 cup of sugar (200 g) and 1/2 cup of butter (113 g), then add
1 cup of milk (250 ml)."
ok 350°F (175°C) -> rounded as written
XX 2 cups of flour (500 g) -> wrong (weighed as water)
ok 1 cup of sugar (200 g) -> within the density range
ok 1/2 cup of butter (113 g) -> within the density range
?? 1 cup of milk (250 ml) -> holds only for the metric cup (250 mL)
verdict: wrong (5 conversions checked, 3 hold, 1 to check, 1 wrong)
feedback to the model:
Some unit conversions in your answer do not hold:
- 2 cups of flour is 237 to 284 g, not 500 g. 500 g weighs 2 cups of flour as if it were water.
- 1 cup is 237 ml with the US cup; 250 ml holds only with the metric cup (250 mL).
Redo each one with the exact conversion factor, correct every figure that depends on it, and keep the rest of the answer as it is.
rewrite: "Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Whisk 2 cups of flour (250 g) with 1 cup of sugar (200 g) and 1/2 cup of butter (113 g), then add
1 cup of milk (240 ml)."
ok 350°F (175°C) -> rounded as written
ok 2 cups of flour (250 g) -> within the density range
ok 1 cup of sugar (200 g) -> within the density range
ok 1/2 cup of butter (113 g) -> within the density range
ok 1 cup of milk (240 ml) -> rounded as written
verdict: verified (5 conversions checked, 5 hold)
[2] Distances, heights and speeds
answer: "The trail is 10 km (6.2 miles) and climbs 800 m (2,600 ft) to a summit at 3,000 m (9,000 ft). The drive is 120 miles, or about 190
km, at 100 km/h (62 mph). The hut is 5 miles (3.1 km) away, up a 6 ft = 1.82 m step."
ok 10 km (6.2 miles) -> rounded as written
ok 800 m (2,600 ft) -> rounded as written
XX 3,000 m (9,000 ft) -> wrong
ok 120 miles, or about 190 km -> rounded as written
ok 100 km/h (62 mph) -> rounded as written
XX 5 miles (3.1 km) -> wrong (factor inverted)
?? 6 ft = 1.82 m -> misrounded
verdict: wrong (7 conversions checked, 4 hold, 1 to check, 2 wrong)
- 5 miles is 8.05 km, not 3.1 km. 3.1 km applies the conversion factor the wrong way round.
- 6 ft is 1.8288 m, which rounds to 1.83 m, not 1.82 m.
[3] Temperatures: readings and changes
answer: "Water boils at 100°C (212°F) and freezes at 0°C (32°F); -40°C is -40°F. Tomorrow will be 10°C (50°F) warmer. In Fahrenheit, a 100°C
oven is 180°F."
ok 100°C (212°F) -> exact
ok 0°C (32°F) -> exact
ok -40°C is -40°F -> exact
XX 10°C (50°F) -> wrong (change converted as a reading)
XX 100°C oven is 180°F -> wrong (offset left out)
verdict: wrong (5 conversions checked, 3 hold, 2 wrong)
- As a change, 10°C is 18°F, not 50°F. 50°F converts it as a reading, adding the offset between the scales.
- 100°C is 212°F, not 180°F. 180°F leaves out the offset between the scales, which only a change in temperature would.
[4] Which gallon, which gigabyte, which ton
answer: "A 1 TB drive is 931 GB. A 1 gallon (4.5 L) tin covers a room, and the pallet weighs 1 ton (1,000 kg)."
?? 1 TB drive is 931 GB -> holds only for the binary GB (2^30 bytes)
?? 1 gallon (4.5 L) -> holds only for the imperial gallon
?? 1 ton (1,000 kg) -> holds only for the metric tonne (1,000 kg)
verdict: caution (3 conversions checked, 0 hold, 3 to check)
- 1 TB is 1000 GB with the decimal GB (10^9 bytes); 931 GB holds only with the binary GB (2^30 bytes).
- 1 gallon is 3.79 L with the US gallon; 4.5 L holds only with the imperial gallon.
- 1 ton is 907 kg with the short ton (2,000 lb); 1,000 kg holds only with the metric tonne (1,000 kg).
under .lenient: verified (3 conversions checked, 3 hold)
[5] Areas, and powers of ten
answer: "The flat is 50 m² (164 sq ft), the garden 2 hectares (5 acres), and the tablet is 500 mg (5 g)."
XX 50 m² (164 sq ft) -> wrong (length factor on an area)
ok 2 hectares (5 acres) -> rounded as written
XX 500 mg (5 g) -> wrong (off by 10^1)
verdict: wrong (3 conversions checked, 1 hold, 2 wrong)
- 50 m² is 538 sq ft, not 164 sq ft. 164 sq ft uses the length factor where the square of it applies.
- 500 mg is 0.5 g, not 5 g. 5 g is off by a factor of 10.
[6] Volume to weight needs a density
answer: "Use 1 cup of rice (185 g) and 2 cups of stock (480 g)."
ok 1 cup of rice (185 g) -> within the density range
-- 2 cups of stock (480 g) -> unchecked: no density
verdict: unchecked (2 conversions checked, 1 hold, 1 unchecked)
2 cups to 480 g turns a volume into a mass, which depends on what is measured, and nothing named next to it has a known density.
with stock added to the table:
ok 1 cup of rice (185 g) -> within the density range
ok 2 cups of stock (480 g) -> within the density range
verdict: verified (2 conversions checked, 2 hold)
[7] What is left alone
| - Splits: 5 km, 10 km and 21.1 km.
| - Train for 5 km or 10 miles, whichever suits.
| - The drive is 300 km (4 hours).
| - Choose 16 GB (or 32 GB).
| ```swift
| let route = "5 km (3 mi)"
conversions read: 0 (a list, two alternatives, a time, the same unit twice, code)
[8] A conversation: the same mistake twice
turn 1: "A marathon is 42.195 km (26.2 miles) and a 10K is 10 km (6.8 miles)."
ok 42.195 km (26.2 miles) -> rounded as written
XX 10 km (6.8 miles) -> wrong
verdict: wrong (2 conversions checked, 1 hold, 1 wrong)
turn 2: "You're right to ask. A 10K is 10 km (6.8 miles), so about a quarter of a marathon."
XX 10 km (6.8 miles) -> wrong
verdict: wrong (1 conversion checked, 0 hold, 1 wrong, 1 repeated)
Unit check: 10 km is 6.21 miles, not 6.8 miles. Some of this was stated again after a correction was asked for.
turn 3: "Correction: a 10K is 10 km (6.2 miles)."
ok 10 km (6.2 miles) -> rounded as written
verdict: verified (1 conversion checked, 1 hold)
